land.text: the Lüneburg half of the Duchy of Brunswick-Lüneburg: 'the Principality of Lüneburg emerged as a result of the division of Brunswick-Lüneburg in 1269'; about 11,000 km2 'including the larger part of the Lüneburg Heath and the Wendland' in 1409

predecessors.note: Otto the Child's duchy (1235) is the umbrella of all Welf lines; the page dates the split '1267 or 1269' in its text and 1269 in its infobox. duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg (eu-09-x) also draws the Lüneburg line as its own land; the two dossiers overlap for 1269..1705 and the compiler should draw the principality, not the duchy, on this land.

land.text: the principality, 'merged into the Electorate of Brunswick-Lüneburg' on the death of Duke George William in 1705

successors.note: Infobox: 'Inherited by George Louis, Prince of Calenberg: 28 August 1705'. The electorate-of-hanover dossier records the matching 1705 gain.

capitals.name: Lüneburg
capitals.note: Infobox 'Lüneburg, then Celle'. The dukes' castle stood on the Kalkberg in Lüneburg town.

capitals.name: Celle
capitals.note: The town of Lüneburg destroyed the ducal castle on the Kalkberg on 1 February 1371 and the duke moved his residence to Celle; the same page says 'From 1378, the seat of the principality was in Celle', so the page itself gives two dates.

correction.text: the Principality of Lüneburg as it emerged in the division of Brunswick-Lüneburg in 1269; 'included the larger part of the Lüneburg Heath and the Wendland' (page, for 1409)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the Welf lands sit in its Holy Roman Empire shapes). The gazetteer region 'Principality of Lüneburg' resolves to about 12,900 km2 against the page's 'about 11,000 square kilometres' for 1409 (ratio 1.17, inside the factor of two). The page gives no territory for 1269 itself, so the 1409 extent is carried back (confidence 2).

correction.text: the principality without the towns of Lüneburg and Hanover and their land, which paid homage to the Wittenbergs in January 1371; the Welfs kept Celle (the duke moved his residence there after 1 February 1371)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the Succession war. Same disc the house-of-ascania dossier draws for the Wittenberg gain of 1370 (Lüneburg 50 km, Hanover 15 km). Reading, confidence 2: the page names the two towns and Celle, not a frontier. The 1373 Peace of Hanover set an alternating regency between Welfs and Wittenbergs and changed no frontier the page names.

correction.text: the principality 'finally secured by the Welfs' after the Battle of Winsen an der Aller (28 May 1388) and the inheritance agreement of 1389

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The 1389 agreement 'abolished the 1374 treaty and secured the principality for the Welfs'. The cadet lines (Harburg 1527-1642, Gifhorn from 1539, Dannenberg 1569-1671) were carved out of and returned to the Celle line; the principality page gives them as compensation Ämter, not as separate states, so they stay inside this shape.

correction.text: the principality with Grubenhagen, which 'had returned to Celle in 1617'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Grubenhagen returned to the Celle line in 1617 and passed to John of Calenberg in 1665 (page). Calenberg, which the page also says George William had to cede in 1665, is not drawn here: the page does not date its acquisition by the Celle line.

correction.text: the principality under George William (1665-1705), after he 'had to cede Calenberg to John, and also the Principality of Grubenhagen'; the barony of Dannenberg 'went back to the Welf line in Celle' in 1671

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, back to the core extent. It ends with the inheritance of 1705.

region.text: the Principality of Lüneburg, the Lüneburg Heath and the Wendland

ledger.note: 1269: the Principality of Lüneburg emerges from the division of Brunswick-Lüneburg. 'When the Principality of Lüneburg emerged as a result of the division of Brunswick-Lüneburg in 1269'; the text elsewhere says Otto's two sons 'split the duchy in 1267 or 1269'. The page names the Heath and the Wendland, not a frontier.

region.text: the towns of Lüneburg and Hanover, which paid the Wittenbergs homage in January 1371

ledger.note: 1370: Charles IV gives Lüneburg to the Saxe-Wittenberg dukes. 'broke out in 1370 in north Germany and lasted, with interruptions, for 18 years'; the page dates Charles IV's enfeoffment of Albert, Rudolf and Wenceslas to 1369 ('William II ... died without male heirs in 1369') and the homage of Lüneburg to January 1371. The year follows the house-of-ascania dossier's matching gain.
1371: the dukes move to Celle. 'destroyed the ducal castle on the Kalkberg on 1 February 1371', forcing the duke to relocate to Celle; the page also says 'From 1378, the seat ... was in Celle'.

region.text: Lüneburg and Hanover, back to the Welfs

ledger.note: 28 May 1388: Henry wins at Winsen an der Aller. 'On 28 May 1388, battle was joined at Winsen an der Aller; it ended in victory for Henry'; Wenceslas died soon after and 'In 1389, an inheritance agreement between the Welfs and the Ascanians was concluded' that secured the principality for the Welfs. The page gives no day for the return of the towns.

region.text: 'After the Principality of Grubenhagen had returned to Celle in 1617'

ledger.note: 1617: Grubenhagen returns to the Celle line. The page's sentence: 'After the Principality of Grubenhagen had returned to Celle in 1617, the Dannenberg line received the Amt of Wustrow as compensation.' Grubenhagen has no dossier; a personal union under the Celle dukes.

region.text: 'George William had to cede Calenberg to John, and also the Principality of Grubenhagen'

ledger.note: 1665: after Christian Louis's death George William cedes Grubenhagen (and Calenberg) to his brother John. 'In 1665, Christian Louis died, and was temporarily succeeded by George's third son John.' Calenberg is not drawn (see the 1617 keyframe); John's Calenberg line is the future electorate.

region.text: the principality, inherited by George Louis and 'merged into the Electorate of Brunswick-Lüneburg'

ledger.note: 28 August 1705: the Principality of Lüneburg passes to the Electorate. 'After his death in 1705, George of Hanover ... inherited the state of Lüneburg, which was merged into the Electorate of Brunswick-Lüneburg and finally lost its independence'; infobox 'Inherited by George Louis, Prince of Calenberg: 28 August 1705'.

wars.name: War of the Lüneburg Succession

zones.text: the towns of Lüneburg and Hanover, which paid the Wittenbergs homage in January 1371

wars.outcome: Welf victory at Winsen an der Aller on 28 May 1388; the inheritance agreement of 1389 secured the principality for the Welfs.
wars.note: The ledger treats the zone as a Wittenberg gain (1370) and a Welf recovery (1388), as house-of-ascania does, so no contest events are added. The 1373 Peace of Hanover set an alternating regency between the houses; the Welfs held Celle throughout.

certainty.note: No page gives a surveyed or treaty frontier; the extent is the 1409 description (Lüneburg Heath and the Wendland, about 11,000 km2) carried through the life. The 1389 inheritance agreement is a dynastic settlement, not a boundary.

notes: Written 2026-11-01 for batch g-eu-b (2 pages opened; budget 2-5). New dossier: Cliopatria has no Lüneburg row. THE STATE: the Welf Principality of Lüneburg (Celle), 1269 to 28 August 1705. OVERLAP: duchy-of-brunswick-luneburg (eu-09-x, 1235..1807) draws the same Lüneburg line as 'its Lüneburg line'; this dossier is the one the house-of-ascania and electorate-of-hanover dossiers cite, so the compiler should draw the principality here and treat the duchy as the umbrella. NOT SETTLED: (1) the split year, 1267 or 1269 on the same page; (2) the move of the seat, 1371 or 1378; (3) the cadet lines Harburg (1527-1642), Gifhorn (1539), Dannenberg (1569-1671) are kept inside the shape, since the page speaks of compensation Ämter; (4) Calenberg, which George William ceded to John in 1665, is not drawn because no page dates its acquisition by the Celle line; (5) rulers omitted: the infobox lists only four reigns (John I 1269-1277, Magnus II 1369-1373, Ernest I 1520-1546, George William 1665-1705), not a full list; (6) wikidata null (not read from a page). Counterparts without dossiers: principality-of-grubenhagen, principality-of-calenberg. The gazetteer region 'Principality of Lüneburg' is the only extent used (about 12,900 km2 against the page's 11,000).
